title: Everyday Heavyweight Crew Tee
description: A 240gsm combed cotton tee cut to hold its shape through daily wear and repeated washing. The ribbed collar is taped at the shoulders so it will not stretch out, and the body is boxy without being loose. Pre-shrunk, so the size you buy is the size you keep.

title: Brushed Flannel Overshirt
description: Midweight brushed cotton flannel that works as a shirt in autumn and a light layer over a tee in winter. Chest pockets are set deep enough to actually hold a phone, and the hem is straight so it sits well untucked. Softens noticeably after the first few washes.

title: Merino Wool Crewneck Sweater
description: Knitted from 19.5 micron extra-fine merino, which is the point at which wool stops prickling and starts regulating temperature properly. Warm without bulk, breathable enough to wear indoors, and naturally odour resistant so it needs airing far more often than washing. Fully fashioned seams keep the shoulders clean.

title: Cashmere-Blend Scarf
description: A generous rectangular scarf in a cashmere and lambswool blend, brushed for loft and finished with hand-tied fringe. Long enough to double-loop without bunching at the throat. The blend keeps the softness of pure cashmere while resisting the pilling that pure cashmere is prone to.

title: Packable Rain Shell
description: A 2.5-layer waterproof breathable shell with fully taped seams and a stiffened hood brim that keeps rain off your face rather than collapsing onto it. Packs into its own chest pocket at roughly the size of a paperback, so it lives in a daypack all season. Pit zips let you dump heat on a climb.

title: Selvedge Straight-Leg Jeans
description: Woven on shuttle looms in 13.5oz raw selvedge denim, cut straight through the thigh with a mid rise. Rigid at first and then moulded to you, with fades that follow how you actually sit and move. Chain-stitched hem, hidden rivets at the back pockets.

title: Silk-Touch Camp Collar Shirt
description: A relaxed open-collar shirt in a washed cupro blend that drapes like silk but goes through a normal wash cycle. Designed for hot weather: the fabric hangs away from the skin instead of clinging, and the boxy cut lets air move. Wears equally well over swim shorts or under a linen blazer.

title: Grid Fleece Half-Zip
description: Grid-backed fleece traps warm air in the pockets of the weave while the channels between them move moisture out, which is why it works so much better than flat fleece as an active midlayer. Slim enough to wear under a shell without bunching. Deep zip vents at the neck for temperature control on the move.

title: Organic Cotton Hoodie
description: Built from 400gsm organic cotton loopback with a double-layer hood that stands up instead of flopping. The cuffs and hem are ribbed tightly enough to stay put after a year of wear. Garment-dyed, so the colour has depth and fades gracefully rather than going patchy.

title: Wide-Leg Linen Trousers
description: European flax linen in a mid-weight plain weave, cut wide from a high waist with a single front pleat. Linen breathes better than any cotton in real heat, and this weight is opaque enough to wear without a lining. Creases are part of the material, not a flaw in it.

title: Insulated Puffer Vest
description: Filled with 700 fill-power recycled down, baffled in narrow channels so the insulation cannot migrate and leave cold spots. A vest keeps your core warm while leaving your arms free, which is why it works as a midlayer under a shell as well as a standalone jacket in autumn. Compresses to about the size of a water bottle.

title: Tempo Pace Running Shoe
description: A responsive daily trainer built around a supercritical foam midsole that returns energy on push-off instead of just absorbing impact. The 6mm drop and firm heel counter suit faster efforts and tempo work rather than slow recovery miles. Engineered mesh upper holds the midfoot without pressure points.

title: Longhaul Cushioned Trainer
description: Maximum-cushioning road shoe for long runs and recovery days, with a broad, stable platform that stays predictable when your form starts to go late in a run. Softer and taller than a tempo shoe on purpose, at the cost of some ground feel. Durable rubber outsole rated for around 500 miles.

title: Trail Grip Off-Road Runner
description: A trail shoe with 4mm lugs and a sticky rubber compound that holds on wet rock as well as loose dirt. A rock plate under the forefoot takes the sting out of sharp gravel without deadening the ride, and the toe cap survives being kicked into roots. Drains and dries fast after stream crossings.

title: Oiled Leather Chelsea Boot
description: Full-grain oiled leather over a Blake-stitched leather sole, with elasticated side gussets and a proper pull tab. Because it is stitched rather than glued, the sole can be replaced when it wears through. Stiff for the first week, then it takes the shape of your foot and stays that way for years.

title: Canvas Court Sneaker
description: A low-profile court shoe in 12oz cotton canvas on a vulcanised rubber sole, so the sole flexes with the foot instead of fighting it. Unstructured and light, with a cotton drill lining that breaks in fast. Goes with shorts in summer and cuffed denim the rest of the year.

title: Recovery Slide
description: A thick EVA footbed with a contoured arch, meant for the walk from the finish line to the car and the hours after a hard session. Soft enough to take pressure off tired feet without being so unstructured that it offers no support at all. Closed-cell foam rinses clean and dries quickly.

title: Waxed Hiking Boot
description: A two-piece waxed nubuck upper over a Vibram lugged sole, with a padded ankle collar that supports a loaded pack on uneven ground. Fewer seams means fewer places for water to get in, and re-waxing restores the finish rather than replacing the boot. Heavier than a trail runner, and steadier for it.

title: Featherweight Race Flat
description: A stripped-back racing shoe at 168 grams, with a thin, firm midsole and almost no upper beyond what is needed to hold the foot down. Fast and direct over 5k and 10k, and punishing over anything longer. For runners who already know they want a flat rather than a cushioned trainer.

title: Shearling-Lined Slipper
description: Suede upper lined with genuine shearling, on a lightly treaded rubber sole so it can go out to the bins without being ruined. Shearling wicks moisture, so it stays comfortable worn barefoot in a way that synthetic fleece does not. Collapses at the heel if you prefer a mule.

title: Tri-Ply Stainless Saute Pan, 11 in
description: Aluminium core bonded between two layers of stainless steel all the way up the walls, not just across the base, so the heat is even to the rim. Stainless will not react with wine or tomato, which makes it the right pan for building a sauce after searing. Oven safe to 260C and induction compatible.

title: Enamelled Cast Iron Dutch Oven, 5.5 qt
description: Cast iron holds heat long enough to keep a braise at a steady temperature for hours, and the enamel coating means you never need to season it. Self-basting ridges on the underside of the lid drip condensation back onto the food. Goes from hob to oven to table; heavy, which is the whole point.

title: Hand-Forged Chef Knife, 8 in
description: High-carbon steel hardened to 61 HRC and ground to a 15-degree edge per side, which is keener than the 20 degrees most Western knives ship with. Full tang through a stabilised walnut handle for balance at the bolster. Carbon steel takes a sharper edge than stainless and will patina; dry it after washing.

title: Conical Burr Coffee Grinder
description: Forty micron-stepped grind settings between espresso and French press, with conical steel burrs that cut beans to a consistent size instead of smashing them the way a blade grinder does. Grind uniformity is the single biggest lever on extraction, which is why this matters more than the brewer. Low-RPM motor keeps the grounds from heating.

title: Pour-Over Glass Brewer
description: Borosilicate glass cone and carafe with a wide-mouth spiral rib that keeps the paper filter off the glass so the coffee can drain evenly. Pour-over gives you direct control over bloom, flow rate and total brew time, which is what makes it worth the four minutes. Dishwasher safe, and the cone stacks inside the carafe for storage.

title: Stonewashed Linen Duvet Cover
description: Belgian flax linen, stonewashed before sewing so it arrives soft rather than needing a year of use to get there. Linen sleeps cooler than cotton in summer and insulates in winter because the fibre is hollow. Generously oversized to allow for the shrinkage linen always has, with a hidden button placket.

title: Waffle Weave Bath Towel Set
description: Long-staple cotton in an open waffle weave, which holds less water than terry and therefore dries far faster and stays fresher between washes. Lighter and less plush than a hotel towel, deliberately, so it folds flat on a small rail. Set of four: two bath, two hand.

title: Handwoven Jute Area Rug
description: Flat-woven jute in a chunky basketweave, hard-wearing enough for a hallway and coarse enough to take the dirt off shoes. Jute is a bast fibre with real texture underfoot, closer to a doormat than a pile rug. Reversible, so it can be flipped to even out wear.

title: Ribbed Ceramic Table Lamp
description: A hand-thrown ceramic base with a vertical rib that catches light along its length, topped with a linen drum shade that diffuses rather than glares. Takes a standard E27 bulb and includes an inline dimmer on the cord. Weighted well enough that a passing cat will not take it out.

title: Acacia End-Grain Cutting Board
description: End-grain construction means the knife edge parts the wood fibres instead of cutting across them, so the board stays smoother and your blade stays sharper for longer. Thick enough not to warp, with a juice groove and recessed side grips. Oil it monthly and it will outlast every plastic board you own.

title: Cotton Slub Throw Blanket
description: Woven from slub-spun cotton, where the deliberately uneven yarn gives the surface a soft irregular texture. Breathable enough to use over a duvet in summer without overheating, and heavy enough to feel like something. Machine washable, with hand-knotted tassels that survive it.

title: Meridian Over-Ear Headphones
description: Open-back over-ears with 50mm biocellulose drivers, tuned close to neutral with a gentle lift in the upper mids. Open-back means a genuinely wide soundstage and no pressure build-up over long sessions, in exchange for leaking sound and offering no isolation. Replaceable earpads, detachable cable, and a headband that spreads weight across the crown.

title: Drift ANC Wireless Earbuds
description: Hybrid active noise cancellation with feed-forward and feed-back microphones, which flattens low-frequency rumble on a train or a plane far better than passive tips alone. Six hours a charge, twenty-four with the case, and a transparency mode good enough to hold a conversation in. Multipoint pairing holds a laptop and a phone at once.

title: Alcove Bookshelf Speakers
description: A two-way passive pair with a 5.25 inch woven mid-bass driver and a soft dome tweeter in a rear-ported walnut cabinet. Passive means you supply the amplifier, which is what lets you upgrade one half of the system at a time. Sold as a stereo pair; keep them off the wall by at least 20cm or the port will boom.

title: Portable Bluetooth Speaker
description: A single full-range driver with a passive bass radiator, IP67 rated so it survives rain and a drop in the pool. Fourteen hours at moderate volume, USB-C charging, and a fabric loop for a bag strap. Honest about its limits: it fills a kitchen or a campsite, not a party.

title: Studio Reference Monitor Headphones
description: Closed-back monitors with a deliberately flat response, made for hearing what is actually in a mix rather than a flattering version of it. The clamp is firm and the isolation is high, which is right for tracking and wrong for lounging. Coiled cable, single-sided entry, and pads that swap without tools.

title: Valve Headphone Amplifier
description: A single-ended triode design with point-to-point wiring and a stepped attenuator instead of a potentiometer, so channel balance holds at low volume. Valves add a small amount of even-order harmonic distortion, which is exactly the warmth people buy them for. Enough output to drive 300-ohm planars properly.

title: 65W Dual-Port GaN Charger
description: Gallium nitride switches run cooler than silicon, which is how 65 watts fits in something this small. Two USB-C ports with intelligent splitting: 45W and 20W together, or the full 65W to a laptop when it is alone. Folding prongs, so it does not shred a bag lining.

title: Magnetic Power Bank, 10,000 mAh
description: Snaps magnetically to the back of a phone for 15W wireless top-ups, with a USB-C port for 20W wired charging when you are in a hurry. Ten thousand milliamp-hours is roughly two full phone charges. A four-LED gauge tells you what is left, rather than making you guess from one blinking light.

title: Adjustable Desk Task Lamp
description: An asymmetric lens throws light forward onto the desk instead of sideways into your eyes, and the arm holds position on friction joints rather than springs that sag. Tunable from 2700K to 5000K with stepless dimming, at a 95 CRI that renders colour honestly enough to work to. Aluminium body doubles as the heatsink.

title: Bluetooth Item Tracker, 4-Pack
description: Coin-cell trackers that ring on command and fall back to a crowd-sourced network when out of Bluetooth range, which is what makes them useful on a lost bag rather than just misplaced keys. A year on a replaceable battery, no subscription. Four in a pack: keys, wallet, bag, and one for whatever you keep losing.

title: Barrier Repair Ceramide Moisturiser
description: A three-ceramide complex with cholesterol and fatty acids in the ratio the skin barrier actually uses, which is what separates barrier repair from simple hydration. Fragrance-free and non-comedogenic, thick enough for winter but absorbing without tack. Suited to skin left tight and flaky by retinoids or over-cleansing.

title: 10% Vitamin C Brightening Serum
description: Ten percent L-ascorbic acid at pH 3.2, stabilised with ferulic acid and vitamin E, which slows the oxidation pure vitamin C is notorious for. Used in the morning it evens tone over weeks and adds antioxidant protection under sunscreen. Packaged in opaque glass with a pump, because light and air are what kill it.

title: Gentle Amino Acid Cleanser
description: Amino-acid surfactants clean at close to skin pH, so they lift oil and sunscreen without the squeaky stripped feeling a foaming sulphate cleanser leaves. Low-lather by design, which people misread as ineffective. Works as the second step of a double cleanse or on its own in the morning.

title: Mineral Daily Sunscreen SPF 50
description: Non-nano zinc oxide at SPF 50 with PA++++ long-wave UVA protection, in a lightweight base that does not pill under makeup. Mineral filters sit on the skin and reflect rather than absorbing, which suits reactive skin, and this formulation is tinted just enough to avoid a white cast. Reapply every two hours in real sun.

title: Overnight Retinal Treatment 0.1%
description: Retinaldehyde converts to retinoic acid in one step rather than two, so it works faster than retinol at the same strength while staying gentler than prescription tretinoin. Encapsulated for slow release, buffered in a squalane base. Start twice a week, use it at night only, and pair it with sunscreen every morning.

title: Bond-Building Repair Hair Mask
description: Targets the disulphide bonds that bleaching and heat styling break, rather than just coating the cuticle the way a conditioning mask does. Ten minutes under a towel is enough; leaving it longer does nothing extra. Noticeably improves how bleached or heat-damaged hair holds together when wet.

title: Sulphate-Free Volumising Shampoo
description: A mild coco-glucoside base with rice protein, which adds body at the root without the silicone build-up that eventually flattens fine hair. No sulphates, so lather is modest and colour lasts longer. Best followed by conditioner on the ends only.

title: Neroli and Cedar Body Oil
description: Squalane and jojoba carry a light neroli-and-cedar scent that fades to skin within twenty minutes rather than announcing itself all day. Applied to damp skin after a shower it seals in water instead of sitting on top. Absorbs fully, so it will not mark a shirt.

title: Ridgeline 45L Backpacking Pack
description: A 45 litre internal-frame pack with a load-transferring hip belt that puts most of the weight on your hips rather than your shoulders, which is what makes multi-day loads bearable. Top-loading with a floating lid, side compression, and a sleeping bag compartment. Comfortable to around 18kg; beyond that you want a bigger frame.

title: Daybreak 22L Daypack
description: A 22 litre panel-loading daypack with a ventilated back panel and a stretch front stash pocket for a shell you keep taking on and off. Big enough for water, food and layers on a full day out, small enough to work as a carry-on. Hydration sleeve and a hose port on the left shoulder.

title: Three-Season Down Sleeping Bag
description: Filled with 800 fill-power hydrophobic down, rated to a comfort limit of -4C, with a differential cut that stops you compressing the insulation from the inside. Down beats synthetic on warmth for weight by a wide margin, provided you keep it dry. Packs to 8 litres in the supplied compression sack; store it loose at home.

title: Two-Person Freestanding Tent
description: A freestanding two-pole design that pitches without stakes, which matters on rock slabs and hard ground where pegs will not hold. Two doors and two vestibules, so neither person climbs over the other. 2.4kg packed with a full-coverage fly and a 3000mm bathtub floor.

title: Insulated Vacuum Bottle, 750 ml
description: Double-walled 18/8 stainless with a proper vacuum between the walls: twelve hours hot, twenty-four cold, and no condensation on the outside. The lid seals with a silicone gasket and the mouth is wide enough to take ice cubes and a bottle brush. Powder-coated so it does not slide out of a wet hand.

title: Collapsible Trekking Poles
description: Three-section aluminium poles with lever locks rather than twist locks, because twist locks slip once grit gets into them. Collapse to 62cm, which fits inside a daypack instead of strapping to the outside. Cork grips wick sweat and mould to your hands; carbide tips and swappable rubber feet included.

title: Packable Camp Chair
description: An 850 gram chair on a shock-corded aluminium frame that folds to the length of a water bottle, with a ripstop nylon seat that sits high enough to get out of easily. Not a lounger: it is the chair you carry because the alternative is sitting on a rock. Stuff sack doubles as a headrest.
